units.function: Monolithic authorization decision engine for board/user/Agent actors across Company, Agent, Project and Issue resources, combining memberships, grants/scopes, instance administration, Agent trust presets, runtime token scopes, assignment policies, issue visibility/mentions, inbox delegation, legacy privileges and responsible-user intersection.
units.dependencyDirection: The service imports nine persistence tables, shared action/scope/trust types, trust-resolution logic and logging. AccessService and most protected routes call its structured decision API; the engine itself performs many live SQL reads and recursive hierarchy queries, mixing policy evaluation, resource projection, compatibility and telemetry in one application module.
units.keyDataModels: AuthorizationActor/source/key scope/run/onBehalfOf user, action union, typed resource union, allow/deny reason/code/explanation/grant, CompanyMembership, PrincipalPermissionGrant JSON scope, Agent permissions/reporting/trust preset, Project/Issue execution policy, Run context snapshot, Issue comment mention, inbox policy and responsible-user snapshot.
units.lifecycle: Decisions first authenticate and separate board/Agent branches. Board paths may elevate local board or instance admin, use Company membership defaults and grants. Agent paths enforce Company equality, special fail-closed skill-test/task-bridge token scopes, resolve trust and low-trust boundaries, then apply default visibility/write, assignment, self/manager, mention, explicit-grant and legacy rules. An allowed Agent decision is optionally intersected with a cached responsible-user decision when onBehalfOfUserId is present; enforcement can run in shadow mode.
units.testAssessment: The previously audited 2,443-line embedded-Postgres suite is a strong decision-matrix asset, but implementation inspection confirms unsafe compatibility defaults and architectural fragility. local_implicit board and instance admin allow every action immediately. Active non-viewer board membership alone allows runtime:manage, secrets:read and decision management; standard same-Company Agents are unconditionally allowed runtime:manage, secrets:read/secrets:propose and several visibility actions even when their lifecycle is paused/pending/terminated unless an outer layer blocks the credential. Visible Issue writes are default-open. Unknown grant-scope keys are explicitly treated as unconstrained, empty scopes are broad, and JSON scope schemas are not action-specific. Low-trust returns null for unrecognized actions, so adding an action without updating this switch can fall through to later policy. Mention text creates dynamic access. Responsible-user intersection is absent unless the credential carries onBehalfOfUserId, can be disabled by environment shadow mode, accepts any active non-viewer for broad Issue influence/skill carve-outs and uses a global five-second cache that can retain revoked authority and grows without eviction. Decisions are not durably receipted; many resource/hierarchy reads are repeated and full-Company Agent scans occur in scope checks.
units.designRationale: Layer stricter controls onto a historically open collaborative Agent board without breaking installed workflows: preserve local/simple-mode behavior, add explicit grants and token scopes, place low-trust restrictions before defaults, and gradually cap Agent authority with a responsible-user intersection.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires one deny-by-default, versioned and explainable PolicyDecision boundary for humans and Agents, with exact responsibility, action, resource, data, tool, risk, approval, runtime and evidence context; compatibility defaults cannot be the authority model.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a small pure policy kernel plus typed fact resolvers and immutable DecisionReceipt store. ADAPT the structured action/resource/result envelope, hard Company boundary, low-trust precedence, fail-closed limited token profiles, explicit scope tests and Agent ∩ accountable-human concept. Generate an exhaustive action/resource/policy matrix; validate per-permission scope schemas; add deny/expiry/revocation/policy versions, purpose/data/export/tool conditions, separation of duties, exact Work/action digest/approval/evidence and version-fenced facts. Keep legacy migration in an isolated adapter with explicit sunset, never in the policy kernel.
units.responsibilityConflict: Authority can arise from local-board/instance-admin bypasses, simple membership, same-Company Agent visibility, legacy CEO flags or mutable comment mentions instead of an accepted ResponsibilityContract. The accountable-human ceiling is optional, cache-stale and shadowable; an active non-viewer need not be responsible for the exact Work/action/data. Decisions are not bound to immutable organization/policy snapshots or persisted as evidence, so later audits cannot prove why the action was allowed at execution time.
